en: The Hymn to the Garland of Letters of the Auspicious Mother (Śivamātṛkāvarṇamālāstotra)
Śrī Sūta said:
Now, therefore, I shall describe in brief the abode of Śiva, wherein a man, by meditating upon the Lord of Devas, attains absolute liberation (kaivalya).
Formerly, the glorious Nārāyaṇa—wearing a crown and having Garuḍa as his banner—performed supreme penance on the outskirts of the majestic Kailāsa.
With all his limbs smeared with ashes, his forehead marked with the *tripuṇḍra*, adorned with ornaments of *rudrākṣa* beads, and graced with matted hair and bark garments—
(3) To Keśava, the high-souled one, whose body was purified by asceticism, there appeared Mahādeva Śaṅkara, the mine of compassion.
(4) Seeing that Mahādeva, the eternal Rudra who is the ocean of mercy, accompanied by Ambikā, moon-crested, and lotus-eyed, (5)
Having prostrated himself like a staff upon the ground with supreme devotion, Viṣṇu began to praise Him who brings welfare to all beings.
Salutations to the letter *A*, the manifest one whose forms are infinite and endless; to the Self of all, the pure intellect, the wielder of the trident.
Salutations again and again to You, the letter *Ā*, the exceedingly pure witness of all things, the Lord of Ambikā, who are unattached.

Salutations to the one known as Īśvara, the bestower of all accomplishments, who limits the power of the world-protectors such as Indra and others. (9) Repeated salutations to the one denoted by the syllable *ī*, the most excellent, the granter of desired objects, who is unobtainable by deceivers, and the giver of wealth. (10) Repeated salutations to the one denoted by the syllable *u*, who possesses a fierce form for fierce creatures, who wields the trident, and who is to be worshipped by the highest of beings. (11)

Salutations to You, the Supreme Self, who are the letter *ū*, the sacred thread, the powerful one, the highest essence, and who are attainable through supreme knowledge. (12) Salutations to the Supreme Truth-Self, who are the letter *ṛ*, the primordial being, worshipped by Rāma in the past, and whose essential nature is the meaning of the *ṛg* verses.
(13) Salutations to the pure Consciousness-Self, who are the letter *ṝ*, the natural state, the eternally satisfied Śambhu, and whose form consists of the elements such as taste. (14)

Salutations to you who are the letter *ḷ*, adorned with ornaments featuring shimmering staffs; salutations to you who are beyond the categories of the signifier and the signified, yet whose very form is the *liṅga*. (15) Salutations indeed to the letter *ḷ*, the place of dissolution, the destroyer, and the primordial cause; salutations to him whose body is as red as a *lakṣa* flower, and who is the locus of all attainment. (16) Salutations eternally to the letter *e*, the witness of "I-ness" (*ahaṃtā*), and likewise the witness of "not-I-ness" (*anahaṃtā*)—the manifest, non-dual reality that is the innermost self (*pratyagadvayavastu*). (17)
Salutations again and again to the one who is eternally perceived as the very nature of the self by those who cultivate the power of stainless knowledge arising from the syllable *ai*.

Salutations to you, the syllable *oṃ*, who are Viriñca, Viṣṇu, and the form of Rudra; who are devoid of both the expressed and the expresser, and who shine by your own light. Salutations again and again to the syllable *au*, who are Maheśa, whose form is the meaning of the great mantra, the Great God (*Mahādeva*), and the manifestation of the measures (*mātrā*) and so forth.

Salutations again and again to the one whose form is the *bindu*, who is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), whose nature is the empowerment of the seed-syllable, and whose essential nature is the knowledge that destroys the seed-syllable. (21) Salutations indeed to the one whose form is the *visarjanīya* (the final consonant), the Great Soul who is the source of wonder, and who is the supreme goal for those established in the *visarjanīya*. (22) Salutations indeed to the letter *ka*, who is worshipped by the deities beginning with *Ka*, the destroyer of the aggregate of causes, and who has transcended time. (23)

Salutations again and again to the one whose initial syllable is *kha*, who is the cause of the five elements beginning with space (*kha*), who is the embodiment of space, and whose sphere of activity is the wisdom of the void.

Salutations to the one whose initial syllable is *ga*, the Lord of the Gaṇas, who is worshipped by the hosts of attendants; salutations to You, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, the secret one, who transcends all qualities.

Salutations again and again to the one whose initial syllable is *gha*, who has the form of a cloud, the destroyer, whose nature is density, and who is devoid of the world-forms such as jars and the like.

Salutations again and again to the one whose nature is the meaning of the mantra *Ṅ*, whose essence is Śiva himself, and who is inaccessible to those things designated by the letters *Ṅā*, *Ṅī*, and *Ṅū*. (27) Salutations again and again to the one whose nature is the meaning of the mantra *Ca*, whose essence is the infinite Self, and who is the nectar for those established in the meaning of the mantra *Ca*. (28) Salutations again and again to the one whose nature is the letter *Cha*, who specifically conceals deceit and indolence, and who is the division of concealing, impelling, and being concealed. (29)
Salutations to You, the God whose form is the power of the universe (*jagacchakti*), who grants victory to those seeking victory, and who deludes Jambha; salutations to the syllable *ja*.

Salutations to the syllable *jha*, whose nature is the meaning of the *jha*-mantra, whose essence is nectar, and who is the lunar orb within the center of *jha*; salutations to Śambhu together with Ambā.
Repeated salutations to the syllable *ña*, whose nature is the meaning of the *ña*-mantra, whose form is *ña*, and who bestows liberation upon those solely devoted to pure consciousness (*jñapti*).

Salutations again and again to the letter *Ṭa*, who is worshipped with the great sounds previously mentioned—*Ṭa, Ṭā, Ṭī, Ṭū*—by the foremost of gods and by the asuras. (33) Salutations again and again to the letter *Ṭha*, whose essential nature is the meaning of the *Ṭha-mantra*, who is worshipped through the *Kha-mantra*, who is honored by the group beginning with *Ṭha-Ṭha*, and who dwells in the midst of the *Ṭha*. (34) Salutations to the letter *Ḍa*, who is worshipped with the great sounds *Ḍa, Ḍā, Ḍī, Ḍū, Ḍe, Ḍo, Ḍai* and with the *Ḍāmara* [mantras], and who is fond of the dance. (35)

Homage forever to the letter *Ḍha*, which bestows great bliss known as *ḍha* upon those men who possess full knowledge of the meaning of the *ḍha*-mantra. (36) Homage again and again to the letter *Ṇa*, which always resounds as *ṇa*, *ṇā*, *ṇī*, *ṇū*, *ṇe*, *ṇai*, *ṇo*, *ṇau*; which is honored by the hosts of *ṇākinīs*, and which is designated by the name *ṇa*. (37) Homage to the letter *Ta*, which is the essential nature of the meaning of the word *ta*, which is itself pervasive (*tata*), and which is worthy of worship as "Reality" (*tat-tva*), being the very embodiment of reality. (38)
Salutations again and again to the one whose middle syllable is *tha*, who is worshipped by great hosts known as *thakāra*, *thamantra-artha-svarūpa*, and *adhasaṃjñita*.

(39) Salutations to the one whose middle syllable is *da*, who is the embodiment of compassion (*dayārūpa*), who consists of great power (*mahāśaktimaya*), who is devoid of country or caste (*deśajātivihīna*), and who is both day and night (*divārātra*).

(40) Salutations again and again to the one whose middle syllable is *dha*, who has the nature of the great elements beginning with the earth (*dharaṇyādimahābhūtasvarūpin*), and who resides in the heart of the upholder of the earth (*dharādharahṛdistha*). (41)

Salutations to the one denoted by the letter *Na*, the Lord of Mountains (*Nagendra*), the cause of names, castes, and so forth; salutations to the Child (*Śiśu*), to the one worthy of being bowed to, to the one of manifold forms, and to the wielder of the trident (*Śūlin*).

Salutations again and again to the one denoted by the letter *Pa*, whose nature is supreme bliss (*Parānanda*), the Supreme Self (*Parātman*); salutations to the one devoid of both the high and the low (*Parāpara-vihīna*), the Purifier (*Pāvana*).

Salutations to the one denoted by the letter *Pha*, who is called the Fruit (*Phala*), and to the host known as the Fruit (*Phalākhyagaṇa*); salutations to the one worshipped by the host called *Phaṭ* (*Phaḍākhyagaṇa-pūjya*), to the one whose form is complete (*Pūrṇasvarūpin*).

Salutations to the Pervader (Vedhas), the letter *ba*, who is known by the name *baka*, the sole cause for the destruction of the very form of bondage for those who recite the single great seed-syllable (*mahābīja*) consisting of *ba*. 45 Salutations to the Lord of Bhavānī, the letter *bha*, who acts as the savior from the ocean of worldly existence (*bhava*), who manifests as existence itself, and who is to be known solely through the word *bhava*. 46 Salutations indeed to the letter *ma*, the sole cause for the destruction of the noose of Great Illusion (*mahāmāyā*), and to the Great Bliss (*mahānanda*) of those who are free from the sense of "mine-ness" (*mamakāra*). 47

Constant salutations to the syllable *ya*, which is the true reality for those men who know the truth as it is, and to the inner, non-dual Brahman that is the true reality. (48) Salutations to the syllable *ra*, which is dear to Rati and Prīti, which is the cause of delight, whose form is the sound *ra*, and which destroys the abode of disease.
(49) Salutations to the syllable *la*, whose essential nature is the creeper and the moon, whose self is the creeper, who is devoid of gain and loss, and whose form is attainment. (50)

Salutations indeed to the supreme Vakāra, the cause of Vāsudeva and others, who is the means for cutting through the snare of desires. (51) Repeated salutations to Śakāra, the refuge for those seeking shelter, the source of bliss, who is as white as the autumnal moon. (52) Salutations to Ṣakāra, the support of the six, whose nature consists of the six cakras and so forth, who is seated upon the six-syllabled mantra, and the cause of the Six-faced One (Kārttikeya). (53)

Salutations to Him whose form is the letter *Sa*, who possesses the meaning of sound, whose nature is existence, and who is the eternal Self; salutations to the Witness of all objects of witness, the benefactor of the virtuous.

Salutations to You, whose form is the letter *Ha*, who is the referent of the word "I," who eternally takes the form of ego-consciousness (*ahaṅkāra*), who is praised by the celestial singers Hāhā and Hūhū, and who is the embodiment of the *haṃsa*.
Salutations again and again to the letter *La*, who is beloved of the great mantra known as *Lakāra*, and who destroys the world that is as flickering as a swing.

Salutations again and again to the letter *kṣa*, whose essential nature is the meaning of the *kṣa*-mantra; salutations again and again to the bestower of security upon those who possess forbearance, whose own nature is security itself. (57) Salutations again and again to the Great Light, whose body is the *mātṛkā*, who is the witness to the knower, the means of knowledge, and the object of knowledge, and who is attainable through the *mātṛkā*-mantras. (58) Salutations to the Great Brahman, the Great Light, who is the substratum of the *mātṛkā*, whose fundamental form is the *mātṛkā*, and who is expressed solely by the great mantra. (59)
Salutation to the Great Mantra, which has become twofold through the manifestation of vowels and consonants; salutation to the glorious Word, which is the nature of the ineffable and the expressed.

Salutation indeed to the stainless Self, who is divided eightfold by the eight groups of letters; salutation to the one who has become all speech, and who is the reality of each respective meaning. Salutation indeed to the witness who is devoid of verbal connection yet is indicated by words; salutation to the self-luminous one who is free from all limiting adjuncts.

Salutations to the Great Light, the witness of all, who is not accessible through means of knowledge such as perception and so forth, but is known through indirect inference, and who is himself self-evident. (63) Salutations indeed to the Great Reality, who is never deficient from his own essential nature both in terms of substance and in terms of existence, and who is directly self-luminous. (64) Salutations to Śiva, who is attainable through grace, who is true consciousness and supreme bliss, and who is devoid of anything superior.
"Salutations, salutations to you who shine brilliantly within the lotus-abode of the exceedingly pure heart.
Śrī Sūta said:
Thus praised once more by Nārāyaṇa, Śaṅkara spoke again with a profound voice: "For what purpose have you performed these austerities?"

Having heard this, Mahāviṣṇu bowed to the Supreme Lord and said: "O God, O Compassionate One, tell me directly of your abodes. (67) Thus addressed by Viṣṇu, Śambhu, the omniscient and compassionate one, spoke to Viṣṇu regarding all his own abodes, which are the lords of all the immortals.

(68) Whoever, having risen in the morning, recites this enchanting hymn—for them the fruit [of their merit] in this world and the next is held in the palm of their hand; of this there is no doubt. (69)
Thus ends the hymn "The Garland of Letters of Śiva’s Mother" composed by Viṣṇu, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.
